business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic system with constitutional law primacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Colombia–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (in force 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF), Ley 1121 de 2006, Ley 1762 de 2015, Ley 2010 de 2019, Decree 1736 de 2020 and Decree 830 de 2021; complemented by Superintendencia Financiera Circular Básica Jurídica and Chamber of Commerce rules governing the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original company registry in shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing a Colombian agent for incorporation and local regulatory filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign shareholder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and taxpayer identification for each ultimate beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn affidavit of beneficial ownership (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) signed before a Colombian notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN/Consolidated Sanctions, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Terrorist List, and the Colombian Procuraduría and UIAF adverse media/links pertaining to PEPs, terrorist financing, money laundering, and corruption; enhanced due diligence required for all beneficial owners and required corporate officers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES (Registro Único Empresarial) through the designated Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Spanish; Spanish transliteration of foreign words is mandatory; the name must include the identifying token 'S.A.S.' and be definitively distinct from existing registrations; names in a foreign alphabet must be transliterated phonetically into Spanish.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may request a one-time renewal of the reserved name for another 30 days through the same RUES portal. If rejected on grounds of identity, similarity, or prohibited token, the applicant may file a written reconsideration with the Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days, and thereafter appeal to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio under the Código de Procedimiento Administrativo (Law 1437 of 2011).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for administrative purposes, but the registered official address must be a physical location open to the public during statutory hours where judicial and regulatory notices are received; a virtual office service enumerating a local physical address may be used for S.A.S. incorporation, provided the lessor accepts service of process and the address is not a mere P.O. Box.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced onsite inspection during the first 24 months due to cash-on-delivery, high-volume retail, and medium AML/CFT risk profile.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration of the S.A.S. in the Merchants Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff under Decree 019 de 2012 scale

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of company books (libros de comercio)
Apostille/legalization of foreign corporate and UBO passport documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Consular office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal and notary professional fees for incorporation and AML-KYC review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial AML/CFT compliance program design (policies, risk matrix)
Registered virtual office address service (first 12 months)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 on the Simplified Stock Company (SAS), Articles 1–12; Colombian Commercial Code as supplemented; Decree 898 of 2020 on electronic registration and the Commercial Registry framework.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Chamber of Commerce of the registered city (e.g., Bogotá Chamber of Commerce) through the Single Business and Social Registry (RUES); supervised by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Constitution Document) for the S.A.S., accompanied by the certified bylaws.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an S.A.S. under Law 1258/2008. The incorporators may set authorized, subscribed, and paid-in capital arbitrarily, but any paid-in capital must be fully paid within two years from incorporation. If paid in cash, domiciliation in a Colombian bank account in the company's name is recommended; no escrow account is legally required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST ORGANIZING RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS / SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY_NAME] S.A.S., dated [DATE]. Resolved: 1. The share subscription evidenced by the capital subscription minutes is ratified in the total amount of the authorized capital, and all subscribers have been admitted. 2. The registered office of the company is established at [full address], and this address is designated as the seat of legal and tax notifications. 3. The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Legal Representative and President; [Name] as Secretary; each to act singly and with the powers conferred under the bylaws. 4. The Legal Representative is instructed to complete all statutory registrations with the Chamber of Commerce, tax authorities, and social security offices and to open corporate bank accounts. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chamber of Commerce through the RUES virtual homonymy search system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the RUES platform, enter the virtual name search module, and submit up to three proposed corporate names. The system will issue an indicative name availability certificate, valid for 30 days. Ensure the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or trademark. Once availability is confirmed, reserve the name and obtain the reservation reference.
required_dossiers: National identification documents of each incorporator
Proposed company names (up to three)
Power of attorney if acting through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, submit alternative names or file a reconsideration request within five business days to the relevant Chamber of Commerce; the request must include evidence of prior trademark search results.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and legalization of the private incorporation document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders before a Colombian notary, or consular officer when executed abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private constitution document and bylaws in Spanish, containing mandatory clauses: company name, domicile, corporate purpose, capital, board and shareholder governance, representation, annual audit, dissolution, and liquidation rules. All incorporating shareholders must sign the document. If any contribution consists of real property, execute the incorporation by public deed before a notary. If signed outside Colombia, the document must be apostilled or legalized at the Colombian consulate.
required_dossiers: Identity and tax information of all incorporators
RUT records (if previously assigned)
Detailed description of in-kind or cash contributions
Draft bylaws in Spanish
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or consular officer raises a formal objection, revise the challenged clause to comply with mandatory commercial and civil law provisions and resubmit for signature; this process typically takes three additional business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chamber of Commerce of the registered domicile via the RUES electronic registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed private constitution document or public deed, together with the name availability certificate and the required forms, through the RUES e-file. Pay the registration tariff and applicable municipal stamp taxes online. After verification, the Chamber issues the 'Cámara de Comercio' filing status and the company acquires legal personality. Notify the legal representative's acceptance of the position.
required_dossiers: Private constitution document or public deed
Name availability certificate
RUT pre-registration if already obtained
Identification documents of subscribers and legal representative
Statement of domicile and land-use compatibility for the registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the filing due to formal errors (e.g., address mismatch or missing form), correct the documentation and re-file within ten business days. In case of duplicate registration, request cancellation of the earlier record and pay a minor corrective fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and NIT issuance with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), Subdirección de Gestión de Registro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the DIAN transactional portal (muisca-web) and complete the RUT form. The system will generate a provisional NIT. After the Company is registered with the Chamber, update the RUT with the definitive NIT and register for income tax and VAT obligations relevant to e-commerce mail-order sales. Request electronic invoicing authorization ('habilitación de facturación') simultaneously.
required_dossiers: Chamber of Commerce filing certificate or Certificado de Cámara
Legal representatives identity document and RUT if previously assigned
Corporate bank reference, if available
Form RUT and signed acceptance of tax liabilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN fails to respond or outputs a 'pending' status, use the 'Contacto' service to issue an inquiry and request a compliance certificate. Usually the issue is resolved within five business days; if not, a written petition may be filed with DIAN.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and business book sealing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks and the Chamber of Commerce (Bookkeeping Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NIT and the Chamber certificate, open a corporate checking account; deposit any cash paid-in capital into that account. If the company maintains physical share registry and accounting books, submit them to the Chamber of Commerce for sealing (pago de registro de libros). Obtain the final 'Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal' to transact with suppliers and customers.
required_dossiers: NIT and Chamber of Commerce certificate
Certified copy of the bylaws and legal representative appointment
Proof of registered office address
Bank opening forms and specimen signatures
Accounting and share records for sealing (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application for compliance reasons, provide additional KYC documents (ultimate beneficial owner declaration, business plan) or select a second-tier bank. For book sealing defects, file a corrected copy with the chamber and pay a minimal resubmission fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Planning Office (Curaduría Urbana) and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) for commercial consumer protection; environmental authority: Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) or the Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) as applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Funcionamiento de Establecimientos Comerciales (municipal commercial operating permit) together with the Land-Use Concept (Concepto de Uso de Suelo).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible / Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the regional Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA (Categoría Exenta). This low-impact retail and cash-on-delivery commercial activity requires no comprehensive EIA; simplified environmental registration is only triggered if warehousing or storage areas exceed 10,000 m² or if direct discharges are present.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: comply with Decree 3930/2010 and Resolution 0631/2015 – applicable maxima: BOD5 400 mg/L, COD 500 mg/L, TSS 300 mg/L, pH 6.0–9.0. VOCs: below the reporting threshold under Resolution 2254/2017. Solid and packaging waste: comply with Resolution 1326/2017 and extended producer responsibility programs if the company sells packaged goods.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Municipal Fire Department (Cuerpo de Bomberos); structural load inspection when storage floor load exceeds 250 kg/m²; occupational safety and health clearance validated by an ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales) under the SG-SST system, covering emergency evacuation, ventilation, and workplace risk prevention.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal www.dian.gov.co; transactional e-services and e-invoicing validation through the MUISCA platform; foreign trade export declarations through the SICE/VUCE electronic customs window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic S.A.S.: the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) is assigned to the incorporation deed upon Chamber of Commerce registration, with RUT (Registro Único Tributario) enrollment completed in MUISCA accrediting the common-regime IVA status. Foreign entity: obtain a non-resident NIT by completing the RUT pre-registration in MUISCA, appointing a fiscal/legal representative domiciled in Colombia, and filing the notarized corporate documents duly apostilled, legalized and translated into Spanish by a certified translator; DIAN validates identity online or via consulate. The NIT-RUT key unifies CIT, IVA, customs, e-invoicing (CUFE) and foreign-exchange settlement records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Colombian S.A.S. is a tax-resident corporation taxed on worldwide income under the Estatuto Tributario at the standard 35% CIT rate (2023 onwards); no pass-through, partnership, or territorial-residence election is available for corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists; the S.A.S. is per se entity-level taxable. Available elections: (i) 'Régimen Simple de Tributación' (SIMPLE, Articles 908-916 E.T. as amended by Law 2010 of 2019) - an elective integrated annual payment combining income-tax components, IVA collection and ICA for entities with prior-year gross revenue below 100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4,979,900,000 in 2025) and no controlling economic group; (ii) income-tax consolidation for Colombian economic groups (Article 14 E.T.); (iii) optional deduction acceleration and fixed-asset investment incentives for digital infrastructure; and (iv) RUT-based election to apply the 0% IVA item as 'exportación de servicios' upon fulfilling Article 481 E.T. conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) - Colombian value-added tax under Title V, Articles 420-481 of the Estatuto Tributario (Decree 624 of 1989), administered nationally by DIAN.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold for legal persons: any entity performing taxable acts in Colombia (supply of goods, services, digital/e-commerce sale or import) is mandatorily registered as a common-regime IVA responsible party in the RUT before commencing operations. For natural persons only, the simplified regime operates while prior-year gross income is below 80,000 UVT (approximately COP 3,983,920,000 for tax year 2025, UVT = COP 49,799) and no more than one commercial establishment is operated; the S.A.S. never qualifies for the natural-person simplified status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance under DIAN Resolution 165 of 2023: every VAT-responsible taxpayer, including COD e-commerce operators and exporters, must issue the electronic invoice (Factura Electrónica de Venta, FEV) with the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica). The XML is transmitted for 'validación previa' to DIAN in real time through the MUISCA API (SOAP web-service with the NIT digital certificate); DIAN returns the validation status before the document is delivered to the customer, and a graphical PDF with DIAN's QR code is provided. Export transactions use the factura electrónica de exportación channel; where the counterparty is in the mandatory e-documentation system, supporting documents must also be transmitted electronically. Failure to obtain validation or to transmit in real time invalidates the document as support for the buyer's input VAT credit and triggers the 1%-of-transaction penalty under Article 652 E.T.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% IVA applies when tangible goods are physically exported under a definitive customs regime (DUA validated by DIAN), the exporter issues the electronic export invoice, and the proceeds are collected and settled through the Colombian foreign-exchange market when required. Services and digital products: 'exportación de servicios' under Article 481 E.T. and Decree 1625 of 2016 requires (i) the beneficiary to be a non-resident, (ii) exclusive use and consumption abroad with no link to local sale of goods, (iii) the provider to be a registered IVA responsible party, and (iv) a written contract evidencing the foreign beneficiary. Software engineering, IT, digital COD order-taking, customer-service and near-shore BPO/KPO operations fall within the eligible services, provided the Colombian entity has no local delivery to Colombian end-users.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA - Documento Único de Aduanas (electronic export declaration) accepted by DIAN customs in the SICE/VUCE foreign-trade window
Factura Electrónica de Exportación: electronic export invoice with CUFE and explicit 0% IVA itemization
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / international transport document evidencing the physical departure of the goods from Colombia
Declaración de Cambio / Inward Remittance Certificate: foreign-exchange settlement exhibit evidencing collection of the foreign-currency proceeds through a Colombian authorized intermediary
Export service agreement or purchase order (for services) identifying the offshore beneficiary, the scope of the service and confirming exclusive offshore use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN cross-verifies RUT export status, CUFE integrity, SICE customs data, e-invoicing flows, local logistics delivery records and Banco de la República FX records in real time. Any mismatch or expiry of the 180-day collection window triggers: (i) retroactive re-characterization of the 0% export sale as a taxed domestic transaction at 19% plus default interest (Article 634 E.T.); (ii) the accuracy penalty of 100%-160% of the tax understated or over-claimed under Article 648 E.T.; (iii) the 1%-of-transaction invoicing penalty under Article 652 E.T. for defective or untimely FEV/CUFE issuance; (iv) customs sanctions, including percentage fines on FOB value for inaccurate export declarations and criminal 'contrabando' classification for fictitious exports; (v) criminal tax-fraud exposure under Law 1762 of 2015 ('defraudación fiscal'), extended to COD wire-remittance fraud predicates and money-laundering charges; (vi) exclusion from the SIMPLE regime and from confirmed 0%-rate export treatment for subsequent periods where outstanding tax debts or violated export conditions are not remedied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (the Central Bank), acting jointly with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for prudential oversight of authorized foreign exchange intermediaries and with the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for customs enforcement and anti-money-laundering supervision on trade-related foreign exchange operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is freely convertible for current account transactions, including international trade settlement, service payments, and profit remittances, provided the underlying operations are properly documented and channeled through duly authorized foreign exchange intermediaries. Capital account operations, including direct foreign equity investment and financial loans, are subject to Colombian exchange market rules: funds must be routed through an authorized local bank, formally registered with Banco de la República, and declared on the corresponding foreign exchange forms. Profit remittance is legally possible for registered foreign investment after compliance with the investment registration and after all Colombian tax obligations are settled, but practical hurdles arise from documentary rigidity, the requirement that the investment be channeled through a regulated local financial entity, and periodic exchange declaration duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds from the physical or digital sale of goods and services must be repatriated and channeled through the Colombian foreign exchange market within six months from the date of shipment, provided that the exporter has a valid export declaration (Declaración de Exportación) and that the proceeds are settled by an authorized local bank. Mandatory conversion into Colombian pesos is generally not required if the exporter maintains a registered foreign currency account in Colombia; however, the full commercial value must be credited to the local bank account or a foreign account declared as part of the forex regime. Exceptions apply for temporary exports, maquila programs, and free trade zones, but they must be documented in advance. Failure to surrender or channel in the prescribed timeline exposes the exporter to monetary sanctions, exchange market penalties, and possible loss of income tax deductions tied to the export activity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Multi-Currency Account
Operational Current Account in COP and USD
Operational Account for E-Commerce Settlement and Trade Disbursement
Foreign Currency Settlement and Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore digital EMI platforms operating without a local license: they cannot legally open deposit accounts in Colombia or provide clearing services without being incorporated and licensed as a SEDPE (Sociedad Especializada en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos) or as a regulated financial institution. A foreign fintech such as Airwallex or local logistics-oriented settlement providers may operate only in partnership with a supervised local bank or licensed payment institution; viability improves if the partnership uses the local institution for escrow and custodial functions while the fintech handles currency conversion and international rail connectivity. The overall feasibility rating is Medium when structured as a BoT (bank-operating-fin-tech) arrangement, but direct offshore EMI onboarding is legally constrained and classified as Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for at least one legal representative with signing authority and, in most banks, for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the share capital. A live in-person KYC interview at the bank's compliance office is required for the initial account opening. Remote opening is allowed at certain banks for additional signatories, using authenticated video calls, apostilled powers of attorney, and biometric identity verification, but the primary corporate account application must be originated by physical attendance or by a notarially authorized agent physically present in Colombia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High concentration of cash-on-delivery collections with remittance attribution conflict between third-party logistics providers and the corporate treasury.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original logistics collection agreements; reconciliations between logistics cash settlement batches and daily e-commerce orders; deposit slips and bank statements evidencing full channeling of COP receipts; internal SARLAFT manual describing cash generation flows; independent accountant certification confirming that no cash crosses internal bank accounts before being reported.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign equity injection from non-resident investors without a clear chain of foreign exchange registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled corporate minutes approving capital increase; declaration of foreign investment using Form No. 1 and Formulario Único de Inversión Extranjera filed with Banco de la República through the receiving bank; source-of-funds documentation for each non-resident shareholder (bank references, audited financial statements, wealth verification); evidence that the transfer entered Colombia through an authorized FX intermediary; validation that the amount equals the CHF/COP or USD/COP amount declared on the investment registration certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected transaction velocity or daily settlement volumes that are disproportionate to the company's declared e-commerce activity and asset base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time order book and transaction dashboard exported in the bank's required format; monthly sales tax (IVA) declarations with supported electronic invoices; logistics providers' delivery manifests and COD vouchers; third-party IT reports validating the e-commerce platform's revenue recognition logic; a clear narrative of the commercial model and geographic distribution sales; internal audit letter measuring turnover against registered capital and reasonable e-commerce benchmarks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Appearance of sanctioned parties, PEPs, or individuals on OFAC/UN European Council sanctions lists linked to foreign exchange payment chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO register with national ID, passport, address, and corporate ownership chart; enhanced due diligence file including World-Check, Dow Jones, and local Procuraduría/DIAN screening outputs; PEP attestation signed by each legal representative and shareholder; trade documentation such as commercial invoices, pro formas, transport bills, and the bank's sanctions approval memo; contractual warranties from counter-parties stipulating non-sanction status.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity investments must be routed through a local authorized bank with a license to trade forex and must be identified in the SWIFT message with the Colombian purpose code covering 'Inversión Directa en la Economía Local.' The receiving bank will require a signed foreign investment form (Form No. 1) and will use the foreign exchange declaration (Cambio) to record the operation with the Central Bank. Amounts above 50,000 USD equivalent are subject to compulsory registration before liquidation; for lower amounts, registration may still be required to enable future dividend remittance. The wire must clearly state the investment purpose (e.g., 'Equity contribution to S.A.S.'), and the beneficial ownership must match the previously registered shareholder registry. Verification consists of the bank's foreign exchange authorization code, the operator's FX purchase ticket, and the updated foreign investment certificate from Banco de la República.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of goods and service imports may use SWIFT MT103 for direct transfers or documentary commercial letters of credit (L/C). ACH and CENIT local clearing rails are used for domestic supplier payments in COP, while cross-border USD and EUR payments must flow through local banks' correspondent networks. For MT103 transfers, a covering 'straight-through-processing instruction' is needed along with a commercial invoice, bill of lading or transport order, and where applicable a prior import declaration and customs form. L/Cs must be issued in conformity with UCP 600 rules and pre-approved by the local bank, ensuring that all documents are clean and that the receiving exporter's country meets Colombian OFAC/KYC validation. Use of blockchain-embedded payment rails (e.g., via Airwallex) is possible but must be layered on a local clearing bank so that the underlying FX entry is reported to the Colombian exchange market.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign exchange forward contracts (COP forwards) with local authorized banks
Currency swaps (USD/COP and EUR/COP) for investment and trade flow hedge
Foreign exchange options (FX options) entered through regulated Colombian financial entities

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Colombian peso, permissible when executed from offshore jurisdictions and settled in dollars, subject to counterparty due diligence and hedging existence
Cross-currency interest rate swaps linked to export receivables or import payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registration renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31 for the preceding fiscal year, based on the company's registration details.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers graduated fines up to COP 4,200,000, monetary interest, and potential administrative strike-off from the commercial registry after prolonged inactivity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April of the following taxable year, staggered by NIT last digit; extensions may apply for certain taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 5% per month (capped at 100% of the income tax) plus monthly default interest; persistent non-filing may lead to tax evasion charges and asset attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by June, staggered by NIT last digit; reporting period is the preceding tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to 10,700 Tax Value Units (UVT) for incomplete, late, or erroneous submissions; intentional failure may be prosecuted under Colombian tax fraud provisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' annual meeting minutes and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate statutory register; evidence of approval to be presented upon renewal to the Chamber of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end (March 31), before or on the commercial registration renewal date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty, but failure to hold the meeting and approve statements prevents legal renewal and renders corporate acts of management diluted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory if the company's assets or gross income exceed 5,000 statutory minimum monthly wages (about COP 6,500,000,000 for 2024) or if its headcount exceeds 200; shareholders holding 20% or more of the equity may also demand a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS (Grupo 1) for entities of public interest or exceeding 30,000 minimum wages; otherwise IFRS for SMEs (Grupo 2) applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual commercial renewal declaration must confirm the current shareholder registry and ultimate beneficial ownership. Share transfers must be registered in the Chamber of Commerce within 30 days; the DIAN final beneficiary registry must be updated annually and within 15 days of any change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays; 50% tax discount for investments in research, technology, and software development for up to 10 years under Law 1955 of 2019; 100% deduction for investments in control and environmental improvement; income from new companies in creative and cultural industries may benefit from the 'naranja' tax incentive under Law 1834 of 2017; CO-SAS entity taxable as a Colombian resident company on worldwide income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) / Electronic filing through DIAN MUISCA portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the 9th business day of the 9th month following the fiscal year-end for entities with taxable income above 44,200 UVT and for SAS entities using CREE; for smaller companies, deadline ranges from 10th to 25th business day of the 9th month. For a calendar year-end (Dec 31), due date typically falls in September of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nombre o razón social / Taxpayer identification (name and NIT)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name of the Colombian SAS entity as registered with the Chamber of Commerce.
Provide the 9-digit NIT assigned by DIAN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos brutos operacionales / Gross operating income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross revenue from e-commerce mail-order retails with COD settlement, net of returns and discounts, in Colombian pesos.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Devoluciones, rebajas y descuentos / Returns and discounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State actual sales returns and volume discounts associated with COD transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos no constitutivos de renta / Non taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income exempted by law (e.g., dividends from domestic corporations), with supporting certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos de ventas y prestación de servicios / Cost of sales and services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report direct costs of goods sold and logistics costs attributable to COD deliveries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gastos operacionales de administración y ventas / Operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include salaries, commissions, marketing expenses, and payment gateway charges; deduct from gross income for net taxable income computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta líquida gravable / Taxable net income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net taxable income after cost and expense deductions; minimum deemed income rules may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto de renta a cargo / Income tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed at 35% on taxable net income; apply any preferential deductions or discounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Anticipo de impuesto de renta / Prepaid income tax estimate for next year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Self-assessed prepayment (usually 100% of current year tax, less previous prepayments) as stated in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sanciones y correcciones / Penalties and corrections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If filing late or correcting prior returns, include the applicable penalty calculation per DIAN statutes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, up to a maximum of 100% of the tax due; minimum penalty of 10 UVT. Late payment monthly interest is the bank loan interest rate (tasa de interés bancario corriente) plus 50%, calculated on the outstanding balance. Formal sanctions for not filing: fines up to 20,000 UVT for severe non-compliance. Extended failure may trigger a 'fiscal stamp duty' and asset freeze orders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% for dividends paid out of profits taxable at corporate level (Colombian source profits) to non-resident shareholders; 10% withholding for dividends exceeding the tax-attributed net profit component if paid from non-taxable or exempt earnings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief (e.g., under Colombia-Spain, Colombia-Korea, or other DTAs), the non-resident shareholder must provide a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence in Spanish or with an official translation, duly apostilled or legalized. The withholding agent must file Form 227 (Declaración de Retención en la Fuente) and present the TRC to DIAN upon request for reduced rate application. Advance ruling is not mandatory; but the reduction is applied at the time of the dividend distribution only if the beneficial ownership requirement is met and no permanent establishment exists in Colombia.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.3% for payments to non-residents (30% for those not in tax havens), treaty rate often 5-10% (e.g., Colombia-Korea 5% for technical service royalties; Colombia-France 10% if economically owned). Interest: statutory 33.3% for non-residents; treaty rates typically 5% or 10% (e.g., Colombia-Korea 5% for financial institution, 10% otherwise; Colombia-Spain 10%). Certain interest paid to related foreign entities may be subject to thin capitalization (3:1 debt-to-equity) rules; excess interest is disallowed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File must be filed if the taxpayer's total income exceeds 135,000 UVT (approx. COP 5,900 million in 2025) or if the value of transactions with related parties exceeds 45,000 UVT; a TP information form (Form 120) is required for taxpayers with a net worth or income greater than 100,000 UVT and with related-party transaction volumes above 10,000 UVT.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applies through Colombia's 'economic substance' jurisprudence and the 'reality' doctrine under the Tax Code (Estatuto Tributario). Since 2019, the Tax Reform (Ley 1943/2019, later recast in Ley 2010/2019) introduced a general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) that disregards transactions lacking business purpose or economic substance. For entities using the SAS model, the existence of payroll, physical or virtual offices, bank accounts, logistics contracts, and a real profit motive is essential; a shell entity with no commercial substance will be recharacterized, and DTA benefits may be denied under substance-over-form clauses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating e-commerce revenue, omitting physical and digital COD sales, or overstating deductible expenses, especially related-party charges with no actual service rendered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty under Article 434 of the Criminal Code (Ley 599/2000): imprisonment of 48 to 108 months for evasion exceeding 200 monthly minimum wages. Tax reassessment of omitted tax plus 100% penalty and interest. Sanciones administrativas: fine up to 6,000 UVT for incorrect returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and directors may be jointly liable for the corporation's tax debts when they are deemed responsible for the evasion (Art. 794 E.T.). Imprisonment and civil restitution for damages to the treasury; travel bans and preventive detention may be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Colombian S.A.S. with no real business office, no employees, no operational bank account, or purely paper-transacting COD orders without actual logistics and collection in Colombia, used as a flow-through vehicle for foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN can disregard the legal personality for tax purposes, asserting all income and credits at the Colombian source. The company may be dissolved by the superintendency (Supersociedades) for 'serious violation' of corporate purpose. Financial penalties: taxable income recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits because of LOB clauses, and a 10% surcharge on top of the ordinary tax if considered an 'artificial arrangement' under GAAR (Ley 2010/2019, Art. 869).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and managers who facilitate artificial structures face personal liability for unpaid taxes when the veil is pierced (statutory in SAS rules). Potential criminal sanctions under Article 434 for fraud. Prohibition from acting as corporate manager for up to 10 years; credit restrictions and freezing of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling COD cash collections through local logistics partners or informal remittance channels without registering as a money transmitter, failing to report large currency transactions to UIAF (Colombian Financial Intelligence Unit) above 10,000 USD or its equivalent, or deliberately avoiding know-your-customer (KYC) procedures for payment intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal money-laundering offense (Art. 323 Criminal Code) with imprisonment of 9 to 15 years for laundering proceeds. Administrative fines from UIAF up to 200,000 minimum monthly wages (approx. COP 5,000 million). Operational suspension and cancellation of the company's commercial registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for implementing AML compliance programs face individual criminal liability if they knowingly ignore red flags, including unjustified wealth, cash pickup anomalies, and high-risk payment rails. Civil penalties and mandatory restitution; travel restrictions and asset forfeiture orders are commonly applied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Filing Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file TP forms (Form 120 and Form 1124) or failing to prepare Local and Master Files when cross-border related-party transactions (e.g., payment logistics services, software royalties, foreign management fees) exceed the thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of 5% of the total related-party transaction amount, capped at 5,000 UVT; not filing at all imposes 10% of that amount. Understating income arising from non arm's-length pricing: adjustment of income plus 200% penalty on the excess tax avoided. Interest from the original due date applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives are jointly liable for the TP penalty when they sign the return without verifying compliance. The penalty is enforceable against personal assets if the corporation cannot pay. Criminal tax evasion charges may be added if the adjustment results in a significant underreported liability.
